rows.b: Examine every plant at least once per Earth day — once in the morning and once in the evening is better.
Better results if you wear Field Gear/armor, pants and boots (gloves don't help) whenever planting, harvesting, examining and giving crystals.
Earned most efficiently via furniture: Bahut (8 storage), 8 or 9 each of 1 Oak Table + 1 Maple Table, your bed, and flowerpots (1 storage each) plus odds and ends. Storage caps at 80.

rows.n: Give crystals on the crystal's day
rows.b: e.g. Fire Crystal on Firesday. Important for Tree Saplings especially — for saplings, always wait for the crystal's day. For all other plants time still matters, but if a plant asks for a crystal it's better to give it immediately than to wait up to 7 Earth hours for the matching day.

items.note: Each plant is thought to have an affinity element; best results planting or harvesting on that day.
Results (what you harvest) are the same for all pots — only the amount varies.

rows.b: Slower to mature but higher average yield.
Mature at normal speed (with Brass/Porcelain/Ceramic/Earthen) but higher average yield than the other normal pots.

items.note: Brass, Ceramic and Earthen pots each tie to a city and give a City Bonus when used in the correct city.

rows.b: Boytz's Knicknack Shop behind the AH

harvesting.enroll: Use a Sickle on a "Harvest Point" to potentially gain an item (or nothing). The sickle may be reused or break with a message. No guild — this is a field gathering activity.

rows.b: Use a Sickle on a Harvest Point to attempt a harvest; the result is either an item or nothing.
After each attempt the sickle may be reused or break, with a message telling you which.
Wearing the Field Attire Set reduces how often sickles break.

mining.enroll: Use a Pickaxe on a "Mining Point" to potentially gain an item (or nothing). The pickaxe may be reused or break with a message. No guild — this is a field gathering activity.

rows.b: Use a Pickaxe on a Mining Point to attempt a dig; the result is either an item or nothing.
After each attempt the pickaxe may be reused or break, with a message telling you which.
Wearing the Field Attire Set reduces how often pickaxes break.

excavation.enroll: Use a Pickaxe on an "Excavation Point" to potentially gain an item (or nothing). The pickaxe may be reused or break with a message. No guild — this is a field gathering activity (technically a form of mining).

rows.b: Use a Pickaxe on an Excavation Point to attempt a dig; the result is either an item or nothing.
After each attempt the pickaxe may be reused or break, with a message telling you which.
The Field Attire Set reduces breaks in Mining, Logging, and Harvesting; it likely applies to Excavation too, since it's technically mining.

logging.enroll: Use a Hatchet on a "Logging Point" to potentially gain an item (or nothing). The hatchet may be reused or break with a message. No guild — this is a field gathering activity.

rows.b: Use a Hatchet on a Logging Point to attempt a harvest; the result is either an item or nothing.
After each attempt the hatchet may be reused or break, with a message telling you which.
Wearing the Field Attire Set reduces how often hatchets break.

clamming.enroll: A hobby in which you dig items out of the sand at Clamming Points on Purgonorgo Isle. Get there by Manaclipper from Bibiki Bay (or teleport via blue HQ RSE swimwear, first sold at Sunbreeze Festival 2008).

rows.p: Buy the Clamming Kit, weigh your bucket, upgrade it, and turn in your catch

items.note: Goal: fill your bucket as close to its capacity as possible WITHOUT going over. Go over and the bucket breaks — everything is lost and you start over with a new kit.

rows.b: Speak to Toh Zonikki and pick "I was born to clam!" for the kit (a bucket holding 50pz). First kit is free; each one after costs 500 gil
Find a Clamming Point and choose "dig" — each dig drops a random item into your bucket. An item in your bucket is NOT yet in your inventory
Every item weighs a set amount of ponzes (pz) that never varies — see Items & Weights
Return to Toh Zonikki and select "I've still got a few clams in me" to hear your bucket's total weight
When done, speak to Toh Zonikki and select "I'm all clammed out" to receive the items

items.note: Clamming Points don't move and become reusable again after 10–15 seconds.

rows.b: Take the Manaclipper (you land at the north beach), or teleport using the blue HQ RSE body swimwear first available at Sunbreeze Festival 2008
One per cardinal direction. East and West beaches have 2 Clamming Points each; South has 3

items.note: Buckets go 50 → 100 → 150 → 200pz (the maximum). You always restart at 50pz — after turning in a bucket of any size, or after losing everything.

rows.b: Catch at least 45pz in a 50pz bucket and Toh Zonikki offers a 100pz upgrade. Same at 95pz→150pz and 145pz→200pz (within 5pz of capacity)
Exceed your capacity and the bucket breaks — all items are lost and you must buy a new kit
Keep clamming with a full 200pz bucket and something may jump in and break through the bottom — all shellfish wash back into the sea. The culprit looks like the Alraune that inhabit Purgonorgo Isle

items.note: HQ swimsuit pieces from the Sunbreeze Festival summer event enhance clamming. Each race/gender has its own set (Lv 1, all jobs). Body pieces reduce 'Incidents' (bucket mishaps) but block handgear; Legs pieces improve results but block footgear.
Heaviest first. Sale prices are approximate (from Pohka Chichiyowahl near the Manaclipper dock) — some items, notably Coral Fragment, sell for more at the Auction House. The list is incomplete.

moggarden.enroll: A personal, instanced garden you can visit and develop over time. You gather materials through activities like fishing, logging, digging, and harvesting, complete recurring objectives, and collect items and furnishings that accumulate even while you're away. Monster Rearing — raising your own monsters here — has its own section.

monstrosity.enroll: Take direct control of a monster instead of your adventurer. Complete the quest Monstrosity, offered by the Suspicious Hume in Pashhow Marshlands (E-12), to earn the key item Ring of supernal disjunction. Then examine any Odyssean Passage to be sent to the Feretory — a staging area where you take monster form and prepare. Entering the Feretory strips ALL buffs and debuffs, including normally unremovable ones (Signet, Weakness, Food, Dedication), and they are NOT reinstated when you leave; Medicated is not removed. Inside, the Equipment menu is replaced by a Customization menu (species, faculties, name). Max monster level is 99, also limited by which limit break quests you have completed.

rows.p: Enter the Feretory. Relinquish returns you to the passage you entered by — not the Feretory, despite what the game says

Exchange Infamy for monster species, Instincts and support effects. Locked species/instincts only appear once their requirements are met. Job-related Instincts cost 50% less if you have done that job's Lv 70 Limit Break quest

Unlocks SUBSPECIES for traded items. Only names an item once you can possess the parent species and are the requisite level — speak to him periodically. If several qualify he names one at random, but any requisite item can be traded at any time
Sign up for / exit Belligerency as a Monipulator. While signed up you can only warp to the three Belligerency areas

"Stalk prey as a monipulator" — pick a field area. Areas you have never visited are not listed, and the choices also depend on your monster's SIZE (shown as the colour of the icon border during species selection)

rows.p: Offers the Monstrosity quest; also explains being a Gladiator
Gladiatorial writ of summons; exchange Prestige
Gladiatorial writ of summons; exchange Prestige
Gladiatorial writ of summons; exchange Prestige

items.note: The Customization menu, inside the Feretory.

rows.b: Sets your appearance, job (traits and spells), abilities and monster correlation.
rows.src: Rabbit, Mandragora and Lizard to start; more are earned by levelling or bought with Infamy. Beast, Plantoid, Vermin and Lizard types are possessable as of the August 6 update.

rows.b: Possessing a monster of a DIFFERENT family resets the experience needed for your next level.
rows.src: A different monster of the SAME family does not reset it.

rows.b: Equip Instincts to enhance your monster. Each costs Instinct Points; your IP pool grows with level and rank. Max 12 equipped.
rows.src: Earned by levelling or bought with Infamy. Once learned, an Instinct can be equipped to any monster you possess.

rows.b: +20 IP at NM, +40 IP at HNM, regardless of current level.
rows.src: ONLY applies in the three Belligerency areas and only with Belligerency in effect. Removing Belligerency reverts you to MON and strips instincts over the old cap.

items.note: Infamy is the currency of Monstrosity — earned at 10% of the experience you obtain, and some is lost if you are defeated.

rows.b: Infamy caps at 10,000 unless you participate in Belligerency, which lifts it to 50,000 — required to exchange for some species.
rows.src: At 10,000 you get "A newfound puissance courses through your veins." and your first star on the shield icon. Above 10,000 you lose none entering/exiting Belligerency, but you also generate no more Infamy in non-Belligerency combat.

rows.b: Exchange at Teyrnon for new species, new Instincts, or hold it to raise your rank.

items.note: The recommended level is the level of the LOWEST monster in the area — there may be fiends far stronger than it suggests, and you can still enter areas above your level. Areas you have never visited are not shown, and your monster's size limits the list. Listed in wiki order; some areas appear at more than one recommended level.
Where you spawn after leaving the Feretory, or after retrying, is random.

rows.b: On first entering a field area — or retrying in the same area after being defeated — you get: Undetectable, Invisible, Sprint, unable to attack, unable to cast spells or use job abilities.
rows.src: Flee to a safe spot until it wears.

rows.b: Aggressive monsters still aggro you in monster form, with one exception: the family your monipulator is STRONG against will not aggro you.
rows.src: As a Beast, Lizards ignore you. As a Plantoid, Beasts ignore you.

rows.b: The job ability that ends your possession and returns you to the Odyssean Passage you entered by (the game says Feretory — that is an error).
rows.src: 5 second countdown; being aggro'd or moving during it cancels the exit. It will not fire at all while a DoT or other detriment is on you (Frost, Poison) unless you have Stoneskin — wait for it to wear off.

rows.b: Examine the true name of an adventurer while you are possessing a monster. Works like /check on normal adventurers.
rows.src: You cannot see the target's job(s) or level this way.
Monstrosity only. Fails on a job ability you have not learned, or where the environment restricts monster ability usage.

items.note: A monipulator needs less experience per level than a player. Cumulative totals below.

rows.src: The bar shows 29,000 but stops one point short: the cap is 28,999 / 996,399.

rows.b: There is no reason to earn even 1 exp past Lv 99 — changing species loses everything over the Lv 99 amount.

items.note: Two types may run in any given month.

rows.b: Double experience from all Monstrosity content.
rows.src: The first 11 campaigns were this simple double-rate mechanic; after those it became the chain campaign.

rows.b: Double to triple experience on chain kills, scaling with the number of chains.
The chain bonus, plus Dedication items are doubled.
rows.src: An item granting Infamy/EXP +150% instead grants +300%, and its 30,000 maximum becomes 60,000.

items.note: Gladiators (players) fight Monipulators (players in monster form). Both sides must opt in: Gladiators by holding the Gladiatorial writ of summons, Monipulators by signing up with Aengus in the Feretory. Both get a special icon by their name, with stars for rank.

rows.b: Complete the Monstrosity quest, hear about it from the Suspicious Hume (Pashhow E-12), then take the writ from the Suspicious Elvaan / Tarutaru / Galka.
rows.src: Hand it back by speaking to them again. NEVER keep it on you: while you hold it you enter Belligerency automatically on zoning into any of the three areas, and they are level capped. Entering grants a 1 minute effect to prepare. You cannot warp in via Monstrosity, but any other transport works.

rows.b: Can form parties and alliances, but only one Monipulator may be claimed per party/alliance.
rows.src: Cannot bazaar-trade or buy from a non-Gladiator; cannot Mount while holding the writ; suffer a 10 second Encumbrance after changing equipment.

rows.b: Only one party/alliance may claim a Gladiator at a time, and you cannot assist another Monipulator who is fighting one.
rows.src: If a party/alliance you claimed disbands mid-battle, you can only fight the player who has claim on you.

items.note: Prestige is the Gladiator's counterpart to Infamy. Seen under Profile > Status.

rows.src: Needed to open a chest from an NM Monipulator.
Needed to open a chest from an HNM Monipulator.

rows.b: A regular monster gives 10% of the normal experience. A Monipulator gives 20% of the Infamy it held when defeated, split evenly across the party/alliance.
rows.src: Being defeated by a Monipulator costs you 30% of your Prestige — it takes 20% as Infamy and the other 10% is simply lost.

rows.b: Drop when a Gladiator defeats a Monipulator; the spoils depend on the rank of the Monipulator slain, and your own rank gates opening it.
rows.src: Possible spoils: Farr Torque, Melioration Torque, Hamrammr Torque, Analgesia Torque, Sverrir Torque, Ensnaring Torque.

items.note: Exchanged with any Suspicious NPC (Northern San d'Oria L-8 / Port Windurst M-4 / Port Bastok K-12).

rows.b: Trade an eligible torque AND any Alloy Tonic to a Suspicious NPC, then pick an augment path. Paths can be changed at any time.
rows.src: Capping a torque at Rank 15 takes 5,980 RP — essentially three Alloy Tonic +2. It was announced that a fully augmented Rank 15 torque could be traded back for a new one, but the wiki notes this is unclear and may never have been implemented.

monsterrearing.enroll: Raise monsters in your Mog Garden. Once every gathering location is at a combined total ranking of 20 or higher and you have employed the assistant Susuroon at least once, speak to the Green Thumb Moogle to start a quest line in which a Qiqirn named Chacharoon visits your garden — after the third quest he becomes your liaison to your monsters. Care for a creature once a day to raise your rearing rank, feed it to grow and evolve it, and collect items from it.

rows.p: Starts the quest line. Sells the items unlocked by each monster's memento key item. Also reports your progress: "Learn about the garden." → "Tidbits of information."
A Qiqirn who visits your Mog Garden. After the third quest he is the liaison between you and your monsters: New Creature, Parenting Style, Saying Goodbye, Rearing Priority, Cheering Effect
The assistant — must have been employed at least once to be eligible
Sells the "Sakura" rank-up key items for bayld
Sells the same "Sakura" rank-up key items for gil

items.note: Speak to the Green Thumb Moogle once eligible to start a quest line in which a Qiqirn named Chacharoon visits your garden. After the third quest he becomes your liaison to your monsters.

rows.b: All gathering locations at a COMBINED total ranking of 20 or higher, and you must have employed the assistant Susuroon at least once.
rows.src: Rank 4 grove, vein and pond + rank 3 furrow + rank 5 coastal net would do it.

rows.b: Chacharoon becomes the liaison after this one.
With rank 2 + "Sakura and the Magic Spoon", unlocks the Cheering Effect.
With rank 3 + "Sakura and the Fountain", unlocks a SECOND monster.
With rank 5 + "Sakura's Excellent Adventure", unlocks a THIRD monster.
Starts automatically. Not a requirement — rank 7 + "Sakura and the Holy Grail" is what unlocks a FOURTH monster.

items.note: Upgrade key items are bought from Zenicca for bayld, or the Skipper Moogle for gil. Feeding and collecting have NO bearing on ranking up — it is based solely on "Times Cared for a creature", i.e. interactions like pet, yell, poke and stare.

rows.b: Release-and-replace to stack more "pets" into one day: at rank 1 pet 1, release it, get another, pet that = 2/day. At rank 3 = 3/day. At rank 5 = 5/day.
rows.src: At 5 pets a day, rank 5→6 and 6→7 take 4 days each instead of 7. You get no cheers out of it, but you rank up faster.

rows.b: Raise a new monster up to your current rank. More types unlock as your rearing rank rises.
rows.src: 1 at rank 1  ·  2nd at rank 3 ("Sakura and the Fountain" + Trial of the Chacharoon)  ·  3rd at rank 5 ("Sakura's Excellent Adventure" + Doctor Chacharoon)  ·  4th at rank 7 ("Sakura and the Holy Grail")

rows.b: • = 0, ☆ = 0.5, ★ = 1. Growth runs ••• (start) → ☆•• → ★•• → ★☆• (many can evolve here) → ★★• → ★★☆ (all can evolve) → ★★★ (max).

rows.b: Gil plus up to four Mog Garden items — Coalition Serum, Coalition Humus, Star Sprinkles, Super Baitball, Cactus Stems, Tree Cuttings.
rows.src: Rewards vary with maturation and affection. A monster obtained and immediately sent away grants nothing.

rows.b: Two items from that monster's collect pool, plus an extra "Put down" item.
rows.src: Growth and time affect what you get.

rows.b: While raising several, picks which monster appears in the main Mog Garden area.
Unlocked at rank 2 with "Sakura and the Magic Spoon" + Chacharoon's Cheer. Select a cheer from the memento key items you have unlocked.
rows.src: Changing to a different effect costs shining stars.

rows.b: A chance each day from caring for a monster, and the chance grows as the monster does. A memento key item unlocks that monster's items in the Green Thumb Moogle's shop.
rows.src: Guaranteed while "beaming with pure contentment": collecting items always gives the memento, and so does any interaction that strongly resonates.

items.note: Once per day you may interact with a monster, feed it, and collect items from it. Mood and growth can be checked as often as you like.

rows.b: An irregular scale from "succumbing to darkness" (worst) to "beaming with pure contentment" (best).
rows.src: Interacting and feeding move it positively or neutrally. COLLECTING ITEMS ALWAYS LOWERS MOOD — except while beaming with pure contentment.

rows.b: An interaction that strongly resonates rewards Shining Stars; collecting always yields the memento key item; and gathering won't hurt its mood.
Entering the Mog Garden for the first time that real-life day awards an additional Shining Star.
rows.src: The status is removed after a day has passed.

rows.b: RENDERS EVERY MOG GARDEN GATHERING NODE INOPERABLE — except the Flotsam node on the beach.
rows.src: Clear it by examining the monster and using "moogle magic" (costs Shining Stars, and each further use on the same monster costs more), or by putting the monster down.

items.note: Feeding a monster anything makes it grow; some foods make it grow irregularly, into a variant of the normal adult form and sometimes further still.

rows.b: Seen when you feed a starter-tier monster at ★☆• growth or more a food that changes its evolution — it means the monster CAN evolve from that food.
It HAS evolved. Leave the Mog Garden and return for the change to take effect.
Keep trying every day — it is not uncommon for an eligible monster to take weeks to finally evolve.
Sheep, Crab, Slime, Mandragora, Dhalmel, Bomb, Dragon Hatchling, Behemoth, Cactus, Wyvern and Adamantoise cannot evolve before 2.5 stars.
A pop-item food (e.g. Savory Shank) ALWAYS causes evolution, as long as the star requirement is met.
rows.src: HNM-tier MEATS such as Behemoth Meat and Gabbrath Meat do NOT behave this way.

rows.b: Monsters gain twice the growth progress per feeding while you wear it.
